decisions.summary: A later plan-review round is admitted, judged as the original spec-fidelity MODE 4 call before review_round_hooks reroutes it.
decisions.why: T315's motivating case was a second round; admitting it serves the request directly.

decisions.summary: In the band: Edit/Write of any file but the handoff, any other dispatch (claims-triage/impl-drift dispatches included), any other target or program, and SendMessage; the main session's resume of a builder past the cap stays refused.
decisions.why: The GM's question asks that a builder be let finish its handoff, and concedes the handoff itself; it does not ask that a capped builder keep writing code. The motivating cases were refused only the mechanical end of their stop points, and the goal sends code still owed to a fresh builder 'as before'. A plan review that returns findings in the band ends in a handoff, which is the behavior he accepted, not a narrowing of the loosening he asked for. The claims dispatch is split off by the GM's 2026-11-25 ruling, so refusing it in the band keeps that rule. Keeping the resume refused follows his 2026-11-26 words on closing builders out and FR-006.

decisions.summary: Past the ceiling the old refusal and its render are unchanged ('byte for byte its old render').
decisions.why: This describes unchanged behavior the plan chose to keep (the request's 'hand off' past a limit), with existing message-store rows left valid; it is not a port held to exactness against a replacement, so the struck exactness standard does not apply.

decisions.summary: builder_stop_hooks, set_down_hooks::stalls and make task-progress unchanged; only the guard reads the ceiling.
decisions.why: Nothing in the request asks those readers to change; a band builder may still stop, and a stall is still marked.

decisions.summary: The band's refusal (wrap-up-refused) is recorded, red-first tested (suite 49 of 96 failing with the branch off), escapable by the existing CONTEXT_OK judged before the band, one message-checked wording naming what is still allowed and the handoff.
decisions.why: FR-012's three owed parts for a refusal of FR-006's guard: a red-first test, an escape of a reason, a message naming the compliant command; all three are present.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] under FR-013 (faster builders' loop), measured by wrap-up passes per builder against the re-read saved; T352 first, then the band.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that makes the builders' loop faster as performance work; the order is a dependency the spec leaves open.

decisions.why: T300's constraint that a choice between the sides is never made for the session, restated per heading. The added stop closes a case the hand script would have resolved wrongly (two main sections); it refuses no case the request asks to carry.

decisions.summary: T419: a heading of another kind (Decisions, notes) keeps its place after the section before it; a join the clone already had keeps its bytes; a tidy plan is never reordered (281 of 285 plans byte-identical when merged against themselves, the other 4 ones the old merge stopped on)
decisions.why: Design choices that keep the merge from touching plans that need nothing (the first build's 9 needless changes, dropped). Leaving existing formatting as it is narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.why: Removes the cause of the stop the carry hit; serves the same goal and the GM's T285 words that tooling enforce the correct behavior.

decisions.id: T419 (b) decide refuses a part B apart (unlabeled by the author as a decision)
decisions.summary: T419: make decide gains a new refusal - a 'part B' section of a task it decides whose preceding '### T<n>' heading names another task - limited to the tasks being decided, no escape stated
decisions.why: A new refusal, but its whole reach is the thing the task exists to prevent (a task's sections written apart), and it is limited to the tasks decided, so it reaches no other agent, command or default. It is not one of FR-012's enumerated refusals (FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011, FR-013), so FR-012's escape-and-red-test rule does not bind it; it sits beside decide's other findings. The limit to decided tasks narrows nothing: the merge in (a) already puts other tasks' apart sections together.

decisions.id: T404 (c) done ref kept outside the clone
decisions.summary: T404: a carry deletes a done commit's ref only when it ran in the clone's main worktree (marks::main_top / marks::same_tree); elsewhere it keeps the ref and says so, at both ends that spend one; builder_done's author-time-and-subject test deliberately not used
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (a linked worktree's carry deleted the shared ref of a done commit the clone still lacked, hiding it from make builder-trees). It serves the 'make land carrying by commit' of T394's line and the GM's T285 words that worktree tooling perform the correct behavior. Not using builder_done's test is a mechanism choice that keeps T397's empty-pick case passing unchanged.

decisions.summary: T419: specs/452-building-plan-followups/plan.md holds 16 heading lines twice, so a carry whose plan conflicts there stops; not fixed here, filed as T423, lands before T400
decisions.why: The stop on a heading held twice is correct behavior under T300's constraint, not a defect of this task's tooling: which copy of each pair is kept is a reading of 452's own content, a choice between texts the carry must not make for the session and that belongs to that feature. It differs from 417, 444 and 449, whose sections are only reordered with no choice of content. FR-009's three requirements are met: why it is not fixed here, the filed id (T423), and the order (lands before T400). Nothing carries the defect past a step: it is filed and ordered.

decisions.summary: T419, T404: tagged performance work under FR-013 (the builders' loop made faster: a stopped carry costs the session's turns while trees stand idle); no engine speed, so no checklist
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that makes the landings or the builders' loop faster as performance work; a carry that no longer stops is that.

decisions.summary: In the wrap-up band every Bash redirect must land under /tmp or in the cap's allowed handoff; this reverses T417's decision to leave redirects unjudged.
decisions.why: FR-006 refuses a builder past the threshold every write but its handoff, and T417's band (the GM 2026-11-27, 'may finish its stop point') already refuses an Edit or Write to a source file; a redirect writing that file was a bypass of the same rule. Closing it enforces what was asked and narrows nothing the GM granted: the stop point's programs and make targets still run, and their logs under /tmp still pass.

decisions.summary: A redirect the walk cannot place (a command substitution) is refused; an unassigned name reads as empty, as bash does.

decisions.why: Corrects a guard message made false by T417; FR-012 requires each refusal's message to name the compliant command, and a false one does not.
